intent: To illustrate how a tiny elite segment of the music industry disproportionately skews aggregate revenue statistics, masking the reality for the broader market.

units.meaning: The top 1% of artists account for $43 billion.
accepted_routes: The top 1% of artists bring in about 43 billion dollars.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The ring centre must read $43b and the segment must be labelled TOP 1%.
units.temporal_anchor: The frame where TOP 1% and $43b are on screen together.
units.reviewer_question: Is the $43b figure mandatory, or is "the top 1% dominates" enough?

optional_valid: The ring is filled to about 30% of the circle, but the chart never says what that 30% is a share of, so it is not used as a value.
The music note icon identifies the industry, not a data point.
unsupported_to_avoid: Reading the ring fill (30%) as the top 1% share of revenue; the chart gives no denominator for it.
Any percentage share of revenue attributed to the top 1%.
Claims about how much the top 1% inflates the average, in dollars or percent.
notes: 原来把环的 30% 当成"top 1% 占收入的份额"，但图上没有任何分母，圆心的 $43b 才是印出来的数。现在表里只保留 $43b。
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
